title: Recovery and Compounding Error
summary: Work through Recovery and Compounding Error.

blocks.md: This lesson follows **Recovery and Compounding Error** in *Physical Data* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Physical Data, § Recovery and Compounding Error
blocks.md: Opening a latch from a nominal centered approach and recovering from an off-axis sideways slip require different physical actions (a later section). Every retained demonstration guides the gripper forward along the narrow corridor centered on the strike plate, which populates the archive with thousands of forward-progress actions. The archive contains zero demonstrations that start from a gripper displaced a few millimeters toward the fixture and return it to the centerline.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Behavioral cloning matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Behavioral cloning fits actions to observations under the expert's occupancy, so a low held-out loss says nothing about closed-loop competence.

questions.q: The section **Recovery and Compounding Error** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Because a physical machine's own executed actions choose its next states and observations, the learner visits a distribution its demonstrations never sampled, so more nominal demonstrations only densify the region the expert already covered.

Every trajectory encodes the sensor geometry, timing, kinematic and torque limits, and compliance of the machine that produced it, so range normalization is cosmetic and borrowed data must pass an embodiment gate.

One command exists as four signals (requested, mapped, enforced, measured) and every pair must be dated at the exposure midpoint, because the tap chosen and the pairing lag decide what behavior the label teaches.
Behavioral cloning fits actions to observations under the expert's occupancy, so a low held-out loss says nothing about closed-loop competence.

questions.explanation: This section develops **Behavioral cloning**: Behavioral cloning fits actions to observations under the expert's occupancy, so a low held-out loss says nothing about closed-loop competence.

points: You have worked through Recovery and Compounding Error.

terms.def: Growth of closed-loop consequences as early policy errors change later states and expose further errors; recovery behavior can limit that growth.
Examples of corrective actions from off-nominal states, rather than only successful progress along an expert path.
